topic: Moser's Circle Problem: The Deceptive Power of Patterns
target_audience: High school students with basic geometry and algebra knowledge

sections.title: Introduction & Prerequisite Concept
lecture_lines: We define this number as R.
Let us count for small n.
animations: Show title "Introduction & Prerequisite Concept" in #FFFFFF.
Fade in a circle in #FFFFFF with 5 points on it.
Draw chords connecting every pair of points in #FF5733.
Highlight each enclosed region sequentially in #33FF57.
Label each region with a count, finally displaying R.

sections.title: The Trap of Empirical Observation
animations: Show title "The Trap of Empirical Observation" in #FFFFFF.
Display points n=1 to n=5 on circles.
Color regions as 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 in #FF5733.
Display the sequence 1, 2, 4, 8, 16.
Show an arrow pointing to the doubling pattern.

sections.title: The Reality Check: n=6
animations: Show title "The Reality Check: n=6" in #FFFFFF.
Show 6 points on a circle in #FFFFFF.
Animate drawing chords between all pairs.
Highlight 31 distinct regions in #FF5733.
Show "32!= 31" flashing in #FF3333.

sections.title: The True Mathematical Pattern
lecture_lines: Regions equal C(n,4) plus C(n,2) plus one.
animations: Show title "The True Mathematical Pattern" in #FFFFFF.
Fade in the formula: R = binom(n,4) + binom(n,2) + 1.
Highlight terms binom(n,4) and binom(n,2) in #FF5733.
Animate substitution of n=6 into the formula.
Display final result 31 in #33FF57.
